solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Lunatic lays (coming from rear) Cyclops on date

indicators.note: coming from the rear means the word is read starting at its back end

blocks.note: lays down = puts
the setter Cyclops speaking of himself is I
D is the standard abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A madman beds Private Eye's crossword setter on a date, approaching from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is the setter's pseudonym, so the setter's 'I' stands in; STUP then I then D gives STUPID.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic as an adjective means foolish or idiotic, a near synonym.

clue.text: Cover for smooth nut possibly out on piss

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements of the letters that follow

blocks.note: the letters of out rearranged
slang synonym for urine

explanation.surface: A drunken bald man is out on the town, his bare head needing covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nut' is slang for the head; a smooth nut is a bald one.
explanation.definitionFit: A wig worn to hide baldness covers a hairless head.

clue.text: Max "boozer tilt" about 99?

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub
a ship that tilts lists
IC is a crossword-licensed Roman numeral for 99 (one before a hundred)

explanation.surface: Max is challenged to tip his drinking hole around ninety-nine times.
explanation.walkthrough: Max Clifford was a notorious British celebrity publicist. IC for 99 is one before C (100), a loose but common crossword Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Clifford was famous as a press agent, an example of the profession.

clue.text: One going on Medicare, vexed about hospital's closing

indicators.note: something vexed is agitated and stirred up, so the letters are mixed
closing points to the final letter of the word before it
about means going round, so the mixed letters surround the selected one

blocks.note: the letters of Medicare rearranged
the last letter of hospital

explanation.surface: An irate patient on the US Medicare scheme complains about a hospital closure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going on' means ranting at length, the definition rather than the joint to Medicare.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who declaims speaks rhetorically and at length, that is, goes on.

clue.text: see 25ac.
see 23dn.
Not one to take the lead but in the reckoning at bedtime?

definitions.text: Not one to take the lead but in the reckoning at bedtime?

blocks.clueFragment: Not one to take the lead
blocks.note: surface: a follower, someone who never leads
setter's reading: the animal counted by insomniacs, which also blindly follows the flock

explanation.surface: A timid follower who still matters when counts are made at night.
explanation.definitionFit: The farm animal is a byword for conformity and is traditionally counted to fall asleep.

clue.text: Royal family party into raised sexual excitement period

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other
raised in a down clue means read upwards, so backwards

blocks.note: the rut is the mating season of deer
a do is a party

explanation.surface: The royals throw a party during a randy season.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' turns the deer's mating season upside down, with the party slipped in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Kiss unusually large copper on behind

blocks.note: OS is short for outsize, a clothing size
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
behind schedule is late

explanation.surface: A big policeman kisses someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' and 'behind' tempt you to a burly policeman and a bottom; they are an element and lateness.
explanation.definitionFit: To osculate is the formal, almost scientific word for to kiss.

clue.text: (& 19dn.) Where you'll get daft answers from Brown clutching rabbit – "I'm done for"

indicators.note: clutching means holding inside, so one piece wraps round the other
something done for is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

blocks.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour
taken as written, part of the scrambled letters
taken as written, part of the scrambled letters

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown is told about a chattering rabbit, and despairs.
explanation.walkthrough: Dumb Britain is a Private Eye column collecting foolish answers from TV and radio quiz contestants.
explanation.definitionFit: The magazine column is literally a collection of stupid quiz answers.

clue.text: Smart arse leader of Conservatives wants bar on Eye

indicators.note: 'leader of' keeps only the first letter of 'Conservatives'

blocks.note: the first letter of Conservatives
a lever is a bar used for prising
a private eye is a detective, slang dick

explanation.surface: A cocky Tory leader wants Private Eye banned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a verb meaning ban; it is a noun. A dick is US slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British slang for a show-off who thinks themselves clever.

clue.text: Member, nuts about stealing?

indicators.note: about in the sense of moved around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A club member is crazy about shoplifting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' and 'nuts' look like a person and madness; they are slang for male body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Member and nuts are slang for penis and testicles, together the sex organs.

clue.text: Bristol-like (round and plump)

blocks.note: first meaning, read whimsically: like a port, as Bristol is a seaport
second meaning: stout and fat

explanation.walkthrough: Bristols is also British rhyming slang for breasts (Bristol City = titty), which suits round and plump.
explanation.definitionFit: Port-like for a seaport city, and stout or corpulent for a rounded figure.

clue.text: Bad Mowlam, as she introduced herself right ahead of the vice president?

blocks.note: Mo Mowlam would say I'm Mo
R is short for right
Al Gore was US vice president

explanation.surface: Labour minister Mo Mowlam introduces herself saucily to the US vice president.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo Mowlam was a Labour Northern Ireland Secretary; Al Gore was Clinton's vice president.
explanation.definitionFit: Immoral means wicked, ethically bad.

clue.text: "God" Boris possibly gets a lesser public position?

blocks.note: the Lord is God
Boris Johnson was Mayor of London

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson, who thinks himself a god, gets demoted to a lesser post.
explanation.walkthrough: A Lord Mayor heads the City of London's corporation, a lesser role than the elected Mayor of London Boris held.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremonial civic post is a public office of lower power than Boris's mayoralty.

clue.text: Scrap a section of Riot Act

indicators.note: a section of means only a stretch of the following words is wanted

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is told to discard part of the Riot Act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a verb; it is the noun for a tiny piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is the smallest Greek letter, so a tiny bit or jot.

clue.text: Prison librarian, say, and what he's doing time for?

blocks.note: first meaning: a job done inside a jail
second meaning: a crime committed with help from someone on the premises

explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' is slang for in prison, which fuses the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally work inside jail, and idiomatically a robbery done with insider help.

clue.text: The people after party funding

blocks.note: a do is a party
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: The public is chasing a political party's funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts the people second, behind the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift of money, that is, funding.

clue.text: see 26ac.
Mrs Thatcher once taking third from Lord Strobes' endless crookedness

indicators.note: third from points to the third letter of the word that follows
endless means the last letter is cut off
crookedness suggests bending out of line, so the letters are twisted

blocks.note: the third letter of Lord
taken as written, before trimming

explanation.surface: Thatcher, in her time, took one peer's flickering lights to task for dishonesty.
explanation.walkthrough: Strobes loses its final S to give STROBE, which is mixed with R.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher was born Margaret Roberts, her surname before marriage.

clue.text: see 9ac.
Popsy Chelsea does possess a mind!

indicators.note: to possess is to hold within, so the answer sits inside the words before

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A surprised remark that a dolly-bird named Chelsea is actually intelligent.
explanation.walkthrough: A popsy is a dated British word for an attractive young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mental self.

clue.text: Lawyers booze (getting end away) and booze

indicators.note: getting the end away means the last letter is removed

blocks.note: barristers collectively are the Bar
sack is an old fortified white wine

explanation.surface: Lawyers drink, getting lucky, and drink some more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting your end away' is British slang for having sex, which disguises the trimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white Bordeaux wine, so an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Uppish American number two has no time for foreign grub

indicators.note: uppish suggests going upward, so in a down clue the word reads bottom to top
no time means the T for time is dropped

blocks.note: US is short for American
number two is childish slang for faeces

explanation.surface: A snooty American deputy can't spare the time for foreign food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number two' looks like a deputy; it is lavatorial slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is Japanese food of vinegared rice and raw fish.

clue.text: (& 5dn.) Popular type of bird on date, Penny, length "relaxer"

blocks.note: a crow is a bird
D is short for date
p stands for penny
L is short for length
something that eases relaxes

explanation.surface: A lady named Penny, on a date with a bird, relaxes at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A crowd-pleaser is a performer or thing popular with the general public.

clue.text: Tommies, having collared chief of Defence, moving forward

indicators.note: collaring someone means holding them, so one piece goes round another
chief means the head, the first letter of the next word
moving means shifting about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of Tommies rearranged
the first letter of Defence

explanation.surface: British soldiers have arrested the Defence chief and are advancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommies are British private soldiers. 'Moving forward' reads as one phrase; split it, as forward is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward in the sense of bold or presumptuous means immodest.

clue.text: (& 5ac.) Congress conventionally adopting this: "Foreign non-believers must be converted"?

blocks.note: first meaning: the standard sexual posture
second meaning, whimsically: the stance taken by an evangelist abroad

explanation.walkthrough: 'Congress' looks like the US legislature adopting a policy; it means sexual intercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday term for face-to-face sex, and literally the view held by a proselytiser.

clue.text: (+ 17ac.) Familiar government minister and what he'll get after the General Election, being one emblem of fascism?

blocks.note: Jack Straw, called by his first name

blocks.clueFragment: what he'll get after the General Election
blocks.note: getting the boot is being sacked

explanation.surface: A Labour minister faces dismissal after the election.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was a senior Labour cabinet minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy military jackboots symbolise authoritarian, fascist rule.

clue.text: Voluntary peacekeepers try retreat

blocks.note: UN peacekeeping troops
a bid is an attempt
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Volunteer peacekeepers attempt a withdrawal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbidden comes without being asked, so freely or spontaneously.

clue.text: Johnny, American masseur

blocks.note: first meaning: a johnny is British slang for a condom
second meaning: one who rubs

explanation.walkthrough: Johnny looks like a man's name; it is British slang for a condom.
explanation.definitionFit: US slang for a condom, and literally a person who gives rubs.
